merger_name: Coles – supermarket site in Plainland, Qld
merger_description:
Coles Group Limited (**Coles**) is an Australian public company (ASX: COL) that primarily operates:

* supermarkets nationwide through its subsidiary, Coles Supermarkets Australia Pty Ltd (**CSA**); and
* retail liquor stores nationwide, trading under the Liquorland, Liquorland Warehouse and Liquorland Cellars brands.

Coles also has a property development arm, Coles Group Property Developments Ltd (**CGPD**), that buys land and constructs shopping centres, standalone supermarkets and / or liquor outlets and then sells these completed sites to third party buyers.

Consprop Projects Pty Ltd (the **Lessor**), is a wholly owned subsidiary of Consolidated Properties Group Pty Ltd, which is an Australian development company with experience developing high quality residential, commercial and retail projects.

Coles entered into a letter of offer with the Lessor in late 2025 to acquire a leasehold interest in a single lot for a supermarket to anchor a new neighbourhood centre located on Gehrke Road, Plainland Qld 4341 (**Target Site**). The Target Site is located adjacent to the existing Plainland Plaza Shopping Centre.

CSA and the Lessor now propose to enter into an agreement for lease and lease documentation to formalise Coles’ existing interest in the Target Site and facilitate the development of the proposed supermarket within the centre (the **Acquisition**).

Plainland is a suburb approximately 75km west of the Brisbane CBD within the Lockyer Valley Region.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. Coles proposes to open a new supermarket site in Plainland,
Qld, where it does not currently operate. The closest existing
Coles supermarket is located more than 14km away from
the Target Site
b. there are alternative grocery retailers in and around the
surrounding local areas, including Woolworths, ALDI, IGA
and Drakes
c. the Target Site is not currently used for grocery retailing.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds determined under section 51ABP(1) being met. The ACCC
observes that the targeted notification requirements for
supermarkets determined under section 51ABQ(1) may also apply,
but it does not consider it necessary to reach a concluded view in
this regard.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
